The motivation was overly simplistic in labeling the relationship as "direct" and symmetric. It is actually an indirect causal relationship mediated by stress physiology, and the bidirectionality is less established.

Revised Motivation:
Depressive symptoms (IDS-SR) are associated with increased proinflammatory processes (TNF-alpha and IL-6) primarily through indirect mechanisms. These symptoms activate stress-related physiological pathways such as the HPA axis and sympathetic nervous system, which in turn can upregulate inflammatory cytokine production. While reductions in depressive symptoms may be associated with lower inflammation, the evidence for symmetry in this pathway is less robust.
